mainTopic: אבימלך and the liability of a בן נח; who goes into גלות (a blind person, an enemy); and how the ערי מקלט were set up
overview: The גמרא finishes the story of אבימלך and שרה. Any man's wife must be returned, prophet or not. אבימלך's excuse fails because אברהם only hid that שרה was his wife after seeing how strangers were questioned there. From this we learn that a בן נח is executed even if he didn't know, because he should have learned. A new משנה then asks whether a blind person or an enemy of the victim who killed by accident goes into גלות. The גמרא traces the מחלוקת about the blind person to the words ״בלא ראות״. It explains that רבי יוסי's harsh ruling on the enemy follows the view that a warning only serves to prove intent. It then settles two ברייתות that seem to contradict each other about רבי שמעון's view. A further משנה describes the six ערי מקלט, the roads leading to them, the scholars who escort the killer, and the trial that decides his fate. The גמרא explains how משה and יהושע placed the cities and begins to explain why the small east side of the ירדן got three of them; the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Must only a prophet's wife be returned?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier reading that 'return the man's wife, for he is a prophet' means the wife is returned because her husband is a prophet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it only a prophet's wife who must be returned, while the wife of someone who is not a prophet does not have to be returned?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the previous explanation of the פסוק to אבימלך. That reading makes it sound like a wife only has to be returned if her husband is a prophet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer linked returning שרה to אברהם being a נביא. The גמרא says this cannot be right. Of course any man's wife must be returned, prophet or not. So a new reading of the פסוק is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: that which is not (here: one who is not a prophet)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about the הלכה of returning wives. It is an attack on how the earlier answer read the פסוק, since that reading leads to an absurd result.

phrases.english: Is it the wife of a prophet that is returned,
and the wife of one who is not a prophet is not returned?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵשֶׁת נָבִיא הוּא דְּתֶיהְדַּר, דְּלָאו נָבִיא לָא תֶּיהְדַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier reading (from before this section) that tied returning שרה to אברהם being a prophet.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'השב אשת האיש כי נביא הוא' as a reason to return the wife.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading implies a non-prophet's wife need not be returned, which is absurd.

steps.title: Return the man's wife no matter what
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יונתן rereads the פסוק: 'return the man's wife' stands by itself and applies to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is as רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן. This is what ה׳ told אבימלך: 'And now return the man's wife' in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reading of the פסוק. 'Return the man's wife' is a complete command on its own, true whether or not the husband is a prophet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כי נביא הוא' are now cut off from the command to return the wife. They will be used for a different point in the next step. This removes the problem raised in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what He was saying to him
in any case, no matter what

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כִּדְאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי.
phrases.english: Rather, it is as Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said that Rabbi Yonatan said:
This is what He said to him:
"And now, return the man's wife"
phrases.notes: בראשית 20:7

phrases.english: in any case.
phrases.notes: Whether the husband is a prophet or not, his wife must go back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּדְאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by rereading the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק (separating the command from 'for he is a prophet')
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wife is returned because the husband is a prophet.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any man's wife must be returned, no matter who he is.

steps.title: אבימלך's excuse is rejected
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ answers אבימלך's claim of innocence: אברהם is a prophet who learned from you. Strangers here get asked about their women instead of their food.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for what you said, 'Will You kill even a righteous nation? Didn't he tell me she is my sister?' He is a prophet, and he learned this from you. When a guest comes to a city, people ask him about food and drink. Do they ask him, 'Is this your wife? Is this your sister?'
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing רבי יונתן's reading, ה׳ rejects אבימלך's defense that he was misled. אברהם understood the danger from how he was questioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבימלך claimed he was innocent because אברהם said שרה was his sister. ה׳ answers that 'he is a prophet' means אברהם was wise enough to read the situation. A host normally offers food and drink. Asking a guest about his woman showed that the people there were suspect, and that is why אברהם hid the truth. So the deception came from אבימלך's own behavior.

keyTerms.meaning: and as for what you said
and he learned it from you
a guest or traveler, a stranger
do they at all...? (a question expecting 'no')

phrases.english: And as for what you said:
"Will You kill even a righteous nation?
phrases.notes: בראשית 20:4

phrases.aramaic: הֲלֹא הוּא אָמַר לִי אֲחוֹתִי הִיא וְגוֹ׳״ –
phrases.english: Didn't he say to me: She is my sister, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 20:5

phrases.english: He is a prophet, and he learned it from you.
A stranger who comes to a city,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out. Either way, the meaning is the same.

phrases.aramaic: עַל עִסְקֵי אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּיה שׁוֹאֲלִין אוֹתוֹ,
phrases.english: they ask him about matters of eating and drinking;
do they ask him at all
"Is this your wife?" "Is this your sister?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יונתן's reading and explains what 'כי נביא הוא' now means.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אבימלך's claim that he was an innocent victim of deception.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The deception was caused by the improper questioning in אבימלך's land, which אברהם wisely noticed.

steps.title: A בן נח is punished because he should have learned
steps.stepSummary: From אבימלך we learn that a בן נח is executed even when he did not know, because he should have learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here we learn that a בן נח is executed, because he should have learned and he did not learn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from the אבימלך story. Not knowing the law does not protect a בן נח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבימלך was told he deserved death even though he claimed ignorance. That shows a non-Jew is held responsible for what he should have known. His failure to learn is itself the fault.

keyTerms.meaning: a descendant of נח, a non-Jew

steps.whatToRemember: A בן נח cannot use 'I didn't know' as an excuse. He is liable because he should have learned.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties back to the topic of the פרק, which deals with unintentional killers and when ignorance exempts someone.

phrases.english: From here we learn that a descendant of Noah is executed,
because he should have learned and he did not learn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a halachic lesson from the rejection of אבימלך's excuse.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A בן נח is liable to death even when acting from ignorance, since he should have learned.

steps.title: New משנה: does a blind person go into exile?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a סומא who killed by accident does not go into גלות; רבי מאיר says he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A blind person does not go into exile; these are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי מאיר says: he goes into exile.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks whether a blind person who killed someone by accident is sent to an עיר מקלט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple מחלוקת. רבי יהודה exempts the blind killer from גלות, and רבי מאיר obligates him. The משנה gives no reasons here.

keyTerms.meaning: goes into exile, to an עיר מקלט

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: הַסּוֹמֵא אֵינוֹ גּוֹלֶה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: A blind person does not go into exile; this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Meir says: He goes into exile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחלוקת: רבי יהודה says a blind accidental killer is not exiled; רבי מאיר says he is.

steps.title: An enemy who killed: not exiled, or even executed
steps.stepSummary: The first view says a שונא does not go into גלות. רבי יוסי says he is executed, since he is treated like someone who was warned.
steps.simpleTranslation: An enemy does not go into exile. רבי יוסי says: an enemy is executed, because he is like one who was warned.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a killer who hated the victim. It gives two views on how to treat him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view only takes away the protection of גלות. רבי יוסי goes further: because of the hatred, he is treated as if he had been warned, so he gets the death penalty.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not just agreeing that the enemy isn't exiled. He says the enemy gets the death penalty, which is a much harsher result.

phrases.english: An enemy does not go into exile.
Rabbi Yosei says: An enemy is executed,
because he is like one who was forewarned.
phrases.notes: The hatred counts as if witnesses had warned him, so his act is treated as deliberate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of killers whose גלות is in question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First view: an enemy is not exiled. רבי יוסי: an enemy is executed as if forewarned.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: it depends whether it looks deliberate
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says some enemies go into גלות and some don't. If the killing could be seen as knowing, he is not exiled; if it was clearly unknowing, he is exiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: there is an enemy who goes into exile, and there is an enemy who does not. This is the rule: whenever one can say he killed knowingly, he does not go into exile; and if he killed unknowingly, he goes into exile.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a middle view. He sets a general rule based on how the killing looks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hatred alone does not decide the case. If the circumstances suggest he knew what he was doing, he does not get גלות. If the circumstances show it was truly unknowing, he goes into גלות like any accidental killer.
steps.whatToRemember: Three views on an enemy who killed: no גלות (first view), death (רבי יוסי), or it depends on whether it looks deliberate (רבי שמעון).

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
There is an enemy who goes into exile
and there is an enemy who does not go into exile.
This is the principle:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁהוּא יָכוֹל לוֹמַר לְדַעַת הָרַג – אֵינוֹ גּוֹלֶה,
phrases.english: Any case where one can say he killed knowingly, he does not go into exile;

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁלֹּא לְדַעַת הָרַג – הֲרֵי זֶה גּוֹלֶה.
phrases.english: and if he killed unknowingly, he goes into exile.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר יֵשׁ שׂוֹנֵא גּוֹלֶה וְיֵשׁ שׂוֹנֵא שֶׁאֵינוֹ גּוֹלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third, middle view on the enemy discussed in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An enemy goes into גלות only if the killing was clearly unknowing; if it could be seen as knowing, he is not exiled.

steps.title: The ברייתא: does ״without seeing״ leave out or include a blind person?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the משנה's מחלוקת about a סומא comes from two opposite readings of the words ״בלא ראות״.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: ״Without seeing״ comes to leave out a blind person. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי מאיר says: ״Without seeing״ comes to include the blind person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing where the משנה's argument about a סומא comes from. Both sages build on the same two words in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads ״without seeing״ as speaking about someone who normally can see, so a סומא is left out of גלות. רבי מאיר reads the same words as including the סומא. The rest of the גמרא explains how each one gets there.

keyTerms.meaning: "Without seeing" – the words in the פסוק about an accidental killer

steps.confusionAlert: Both sages quote the exact same words, ״בלא ראות״, yet they reach opposite conclusions. Don't assume one of them is reading a different פסוק.

phrases.english: גמרא:
The Rabbis taught:
"Without seeing" – to exclude a blind person,
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:23

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Meir says:
"Without seeing" – to include the blind person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא source behind the משנה's מחלוקת about a סומא (step 5).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: ״בלא ראות״ excludes a סומא from גלות. רבי מאיר: ״בלא ראות״ includes a סומא.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה gets an exclusion out of ״בלא ראות״.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks for the logic behind רבי יהודה's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An exclusion only makes sense if something else would otherwise have included the סומא. The גמרא wants to know what that is.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבי יהודה's view in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יהודה reads ״בלא ראות״ as an exclusion of a סומא.

steps.title: The forest פסוק includes everyone, and ״without seeing״ takes the blind person out
steps.stepSummary: The general פסוק about going into the forest would include even a סומא, so ״בלא ראות״ comes to exclude him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: ״And one who goes with his neighbor into the forest״. That would include even a blind person. Then ״without seeing״ comes and excludes him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a different פסוק, about the forest, is general and would include a סומא. ״בלא ראות״ then narrows it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה there is one broad פסוק and one limiting phrase. The broad פסוק includes everyone who kills by accident. ״בלא ראות״ limits it to someone who could normally see, so the סומא is out.

keyTerms.meaning: In the forest – the example case of accidental killing in דברים

phrases.english: as it is written: "And one who comes with his neighbor into the forest" –
phrases.notes: דברים 19:5

phrases.english: even a blind person is included.
"Without seeing" came and excluded him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The forest פסוק is general and would include a סומא. ״בלא ראות״ limits it and excludes him.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: two limiting phrases in a row actually include
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says both ״בלא ראות״ and ״בבלי דעת״ are limiting phrases. One limit after another limit works to include, so a סומא is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר says: ״Without seeing״ comes to exclude, and ״without knowledge״ comes to exclude. That makes a limit after a limit, and a limit after a limit only comes to include.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי מאיר's reasoning. He uses the rule that two limiting phrases in a row actually add cases instead of taking them away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר agrees that ״בלא ראות״ on its own would exclude a סומא. But ״בבלי דעת״ is a second limiting phrase. By the rule of מיעוט אחר מיעוט, the two together include the סומא in גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: "Without knowledge" – another phrase in the פסוקים of the accidental killer
A limiting phrase after a limiting phrase

keyTerms.term: אֵין מִיעוּט אַחַר מִיעוּט אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת
keyTerms.meaning: Two limits in a row only come to include (a rule of דרשה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic rule of reading the תורה: two limiting words in a row cancel each other out and end up adding cases.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir says:
"Without seeing" – to exclude,
"without knowledge" – to exclude,
phrases.notes: דברים 19:4

phrases.english: that is a limit after a limit,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מִיעוּט אַחַר מִיעוּט אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת.
phrases.english: and a limit after a limit comes only to include.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי מאיר's reading in place of רבי יהודה's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״בלא ראות״ and ״בבלי דעת״ are two limits in a row, and that includes a סומא in גלות.

steps.title: How does רבי יהודה handle the double limit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה deals with רבי מאיר's argument from the two limiting phrases.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה with רבי מאיר's argument. If there really are two limits in a row, רבי יהודה should have to include the סומא too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This one-word challenge pushes רבי יהודה to explain ״בבלי דעת″. If that phrase also limits the סומא, the double-limit rule would defeat his view.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda – how does he respond?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי מאיר's double-limit argument against רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's exclusion of a סומא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ״בבלי דעת״ is a second limit, then by the rule of מיעוט אחר מיעוט the סומא should be included.

steps.title: ״Without knowledge״ comes to leave out someone with intent
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says ״בבלי דעת״ is not a second limit on the סומא. It comes to leave out someone who acted with intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: ״Without knowledge״ comes to exclude someone who acted with intent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers that ״בבלי דעת״ has its own separate job, so there is no double limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double-limit rule only works when both phrases limit the same thing. For רבי יהודה, ״בלא ראות״ excludes a סומא and ״בבלי דעת״ excludes someone with intent. They limit two different cases, so the rule does not apply.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: one broad פסוק plus ״בלא ראות״ excludes a סומא, and ״בבלי דעת״ excludes someone with intent. רבי מאיר: ״בלא ראות״ and ״בבלי דעת״ are two limits in a row, so a סומא is included in גלות.

phrases.english: "Without knowledge" comes to exclude one who acted with intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the second phrase a different job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״בבלי דעת״ is a second limit on the סומא, which would make a double limit.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״בבלי דעת״ excludes someone with intent, a different case, so there is no double limit.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי יוסי on the enemy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's ruling from the משנה that an enemy who kills is executed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: the enemy is executed, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes רבי יוסי's opinion. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוסי says that if a שונא kills someone, he is executed. That is a harsh ruling, so the גמרא quotes it in order to question it.

keyTerms.meaning: An enemy, someone who hated the victim

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says
The enemy is executed, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion about the סומא and returns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, an enemy who kills is executed.

steps.title: But he was never warned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: how can the enemy be executed if no one gave him התראה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But they did not warn him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי. Normally בית דין cannot execute anyone unless he was warned first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A basic rule is that punishment requires התראה, a warning given just before the sin. In this case nobody warned the enemy, so it seems he should not be executed.

keyTerms.meaning: The warning that must be given right before a sin for בית דין to punish

phrases.english: But they did not warn him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's ruling that an enemy who kills is executed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Execution requires התראה, and here there was none.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה, who says a חבר needs no warning, because a warning only exists to tell accidental from deliberate.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה. A ברייתא teaches that he says: a חבר does not need a warning, because a warning only exists to tell apart someone who acted by accident from someone who acted on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this משנה follows a sage who holds that a warning is not always needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי בר יהודה, the whole point of התראה is to show that the person sinned on purpose. If we already know he acted on purpose, as with a knowledgeable חבר, no warning is needed. In the same way, the enemy's hatred shows that he acted deliberately.

keyTerms.meaning: A learned person who is careful about מצוות and knows the הלכה
Doing something by accident or without knowing

steps.whyThisMatters: This step shows that for this sage, התראה is a way of proving intent, not a requirement for its own sake.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה הִיא,
phrases.english: Our mishnah follows Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda,
as it was taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:
A chaver does not need a warning,
because the warning was not given
except to tell apart accidental from deliberate.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא about the missing warning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying which sage the משנה follows
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every person must be warned before he can be punished.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוסי בר יהודה, a warning only proves intent, so when intent is already clear, no warning is needed.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: when an enemy is exiled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's view from the משנה, and a ברייתא explains it: if the rope snapped, he is exiled; if the object slipped, he is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: there is an enemy who goes into exile, and so on. A ברייתא teaches: what did רבי שמעון mean when he said some enemies are exiled and some are not? If the rope snapped, he is exiled. If the object slipped from his hand, he is not exiled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to רבי שמעון's opinion in the משנה. It brings a ברייתא that explains which enemy goes to exile and which does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a rope snaps, it looks like a real accident, so the enemy gets the regular גלות. When the object slips from his own hand, we suspect that he let it go on purpose, so גלות is not enough for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes into exile to a city of refuge, the punishment for killing by accident
Slipped or was let go from his hand

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
There is an enemy who is exiled, etc.
It was taught in a baraita:
In what case did Rabbi Shimon say
there is an enemy who is exiled
and there is an enemy who is not exiled?
If it snapped, he is exiled;
phrases.notes: The rope holding the object broke, so it fell and killed someone.

phrases.english: if it slipped, he is not exiled.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן יֵשׁ שׂוֹנֵא גּוֹלֶה וְיֵשׁ שׂוֹנֵא שֶׁאֵינוֹ גּוֹלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next opinion in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For an enemy: if the rope snapped, he is exiled; if the object slipped, he is not exiled.

steps.title: A second ברייתא says the opposite
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון as saying a person is only exiled if the object slipped, which contradicts the first ברייתא on both cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: But another ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון says: a person is never exiled unless his trowel slipped from his hand. So 'snapped' contradicts 'snapped,' and 'slipped' contradicts 'slipped'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two ברייתות quote רבי שמעון in opposite ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא says: snapped means exile, slipped means no exile. The second says only 'slipped' leads to exile, which means 'snapped' does not. The two ברייתות are exactly reversed.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
He is never exiled
unless his trowel slips from his hand.
'Snapped' contradicts 'snapped',
phrases.notes: He means the 'snapped' case in one ברייתא clashes with the 'snapped' case in the other.

phrases.english: 'slipped' contradicts 'slipped'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ גּוֹלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא just quoted, using another ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first ברייתא's explanation of רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות in רבי שמעון's name give opposite results for both the 'snapped' and the 'slipped' cases.

steps.title: Snapped: friend versus enemy
steps.stepSummary: The 'snapped' contradiction is solved: the second ברייתא is about a friend, and the first is about an enemy.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Snapped' against 'snapped' is not a problem. This ברייתא is about a friend, and that one is about an enemy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first half of the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות are talking about different people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a friend (אוהב), a snapped rope is a complete accident he could not control, so he is not even exiled. For an enemy, we cannot treat it as a complete accident, so he is exiled. The next step answers the 'slipped' contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: This one ... and that one (two different cases)

steps.confusionAlert: This answer only solves the 'snapped' contradiction. The 'slipped' contradiction is answered separately in the next step.

phrases.english: 'Snapped' against 'snapped' is not a problem:
this one is about a friend,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the second ברייתא, where a snapped rope means no exile.

phrases.english: and that one is about an enemy.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִפְסַק אַנִּפְסַק לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא בְּאוֹהֵב וְהָא בְּשׂוֹנֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the contradiction raised in the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each ברייתא is about a different kind of person
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות are about the same kind of killer, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: A friend whose rope snapped is not exiled because it was a complete accident; an enemy whose rope snapped is exiled.

steps.title: The 'slipped' contradiction depends on רבי versus רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The second contradiction, about an object that slipped, is solved by saying each ברייתא follows a different תנא: one follows רבי, the other follows רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Slipped' against 'slipped' is not a problem: this ברייתא follows רבי, and that one follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second half of the contradiction from step 18, the case where the object slipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier משנה, רבי said that if an ax-head slips off its handle and kills someone, the person is not exiled, while the רבנן said he is exiled. One ברייתא reports רבי שמעון's view the way רבי would have it, and the other reports it the way the רבנן would have it. So the two ברייתות are not really arguing about what רבי שמעון holds in the same framework.

keyTerms.meaning: slipped off (the ax-head came loose from its handle)
it is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
the majority Sages who disagree with רבי

steps.whatToRemember: Both halves of the contradiction are now solved. 'Snapped' is solved by friend versus enemy, and 'slipped' is solved by רבי versus רבנן.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה. He is not רבי שמעון, whose view the ברייתות are reporting.

phrases.english: 'Slipped' against 'slipped'
phrases.notes: This is the second contradiction: the case where the ax-head slipped off its handle.

phrases.english: is not difficult:
this one follows רבי,
and that one follows the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer begun in step 19 by solving the second half of the contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different תנאים: each ברייתא follows a different view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to report רבי שמעון's view on a slipped object in opposite ways.
steps.terutzMaskana: One ברייתא follows רבי's approach and the other follows the רבנן's approach, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: The killer is exiled to six cities of refuge
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that killers are exiled to ערי מקלט: three across the ירדן and three in ארץ כנען.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Where are they exiled to? To the ערי מקלט: three across the ירדן and three in the land of כנען. As the פסוק says: 'Three cities you shall give across the ירדן, and three cities you shall give in the land of כנען.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It answers where someone who killed by accident must go into exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is six special cities called ערי מקלט, split evenly between the east bank of the ירדן and ארץ ישראל proper. The משנה brings a פסוק that spells out this three-and-three division.

keyTerms.meaning: cities of refuge, where an accidental killer is protected
the land across (east of) the ירדן river

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a whole new section about how the ערי מקלט system actually works.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
To where are they exiled?
To the cities of refuge,
to the three across the Jordan
and to the three in the land of Canaan.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אֵת שְׁלֹשׁ הֶעָרִים תִּתְּנוּ מֵעֵבֶר לַיַּרְדֵּן
phrases.english: As it says: 'Three cities you shall give across the Jordan
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:14

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵת שְׁלֹשׁ הֶעָרִים תִּתְּנוּ בְּאֶרֶץ כְּנָעַן וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: and three cities you shall give in the land of Canaan, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Accidental killers are exiled to six ערי מקלט, three on each side of the ירדן.

steps.title: The cities only protected once all six were set up
steps.stepSummary: The three cities across the ירדן did not protect anyone until the three in ארץ ישראל were also chosen, because all six had to work together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until the three in ארץ ישראל were chosen, the three across the ירדן did not take anyone in. As it says: 'Six ערי מקלט they shall be,' which teaches that they work only once all six take people in together.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a timing rule: the cities across the ירדן were not yet active on their own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the three cities across the ירדן were chosen first, they could not protect anyone yet. The פסוק calls them 'six' cities, so the system only begins once all six are in place at the same time.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְחֲרוּ שָׁלֹשׁ שֶׁבְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: Until the three in the Land of Israel were chosen,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיוּ שָׁלֹשׁ שֶׁבְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן קוֹלְטוֹת,
phrases.english: the three across the Jordan did not take anyone in,
as it says: 'Six cities of refuge they shall be' –
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:13

phrases.english: not until all six of them take people in together.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְחֲרוּ שָׁלֹשׁ שֶׁבְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a rule about when the six cities from step 21 began to work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערי מקלט only protect once all six are designated and functioning together.

steps.title: Roads were prepared leading to the cities
steps.stepSummary: Clear roads were set up leading to the ערי מקלט, based on the פסוק 'Prepare for yourself the road.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And roads were prepared for them from one place to another, as it says: 'Prepare for yourself the road, and divide into three, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה says roads were laid out so the killer could easily reach a עיר מקלט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The killer has to run to safety quickly. The פסוק tells us to 'prepare the road,' so the roads to these cities were kept straight and clear.

keyTerms.meaning: set up, made straight and ready
and you shall divide into three

phrases.english: And roads were prepared for them
from this one to that one,
phrases.notes: He means roads leading from place to place toward the cities, so the way there is clear.

phrases.english: as it says: 'Prepare for yourself the road,
phrases.notes: דברים 19:3

phrases.english: and divide into three, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with another practical rule about the cities.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roads leading to the ערי מקלט must be prepared and kept clear.

steps.title: Two scholars escort the killer, and רבי מאיר says he speaks for himself too
steps.stepSummary: Two תלמידי חכמים travel with the killer so they can talk the avenger out of killing him. רבי מאיר adds that the killer speaks up for himself as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: They give him two תלמידי חכמים, in case the avenger tries to kill him on the road, so they can speak to the avenger. רבי מאיר says: he also speaks for himself, as it says: 'And this is the matter of the killer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes an escort of two scholars for the killer's trip to the עיר מקלט, and then brings רבי מאיר's addition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger is that the גואל הדם (the victim's relative) might attack the killer on the way. The scholars' job is to persuade him to back off. רבי מאיר reads the word 'דבר' in the פסוק as 'speaking,' which teaches that the killer can also plead his own case.

keyTerms.meaning: they hand over, assign (as an escort)
by himself, on his own behalf

steps.whatToRemember: The killer is helped on every level: the cities themselves, clear roads, and an escort of two scholars to protect him on the way.

phrases.english: And they assign them two Torah scholars,
in case he kills him on the road,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the גואל הדם, the victim's relative who wants revenge. The משנה doesn't name him, but that's who is meant.

phrases.english: and they will speak to him.
Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף הוּא מְדַבֵּר עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: He also speaks on his own behalf,
phrases.notes: 'He' here is the killer himself.

phrases.english: as it says: 'And this is the matter of the killer.'
phrases.notes: דברים 19:4. רבי מאיר reads 'דבר' as 'speech,' meaning the killer's own words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with another protection given to the fleeing killer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two תלמידי חכמים escort the killer to persuade the avenger. רבי מאיר holds that the killer also speaks for himself.

steps.title: Every killer first runs to a city of refuge, and the court then decides his fate
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר יהודה teaches that both the accidental killer and the deliberate killer would first run to an עיר מקלט. The court then brought him back for trial and ruled: death, freedom, or return to exile.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: At first, whether he killed by accident or on purpose, the killer runs ahead to the cities of refuge. Then the court sends for him and brings him back from there. If he is found deserving of death in court, they execute him. If he is not found deserving of death, they free him. If he is found deserving of exile, they send him back to his place, as the פסוק says: 'And the congregation shall return him to his city of refuge.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with רבי יוסי בר יהודה, who explains that every killer runs to the city of refuge first, before any trial. Afterward the court brings him back, judges him, and decides what happens to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The city of refuge is a safe place to wait before the trial, not only for killers already proven to be accidental. After the trial there are three possible outcomes: a מזיד is executed, a killer found not liable at all goes free, and a שוגג is sent back to exile. The proof is the word 'return' (והשיבו) in the פסוק, which shows he was already in the city before the trial.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who killed by accident, without meaning to
They run ahead, getting there first, before the trial
Exile to a city of refuge, the punishment for an accidental killer
They set him free, with no punishment

steps.whatToRemember: Every killer, whether accidental or deliberate, first runs to an עיר מקלט. The court then brings him back for trial. The result is death, freedom, or a return to exile.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the city of refuge protects a deliberate killer forever. It only shelters him until the court can bring him back and judge him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:
At first, both the accidental killer and the deliberate killer
run ahead to the cities of refuge,
phrases.notes: He means before any trial has happened, the killer escapes there right away.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית דִּין שׁוֹלְחִין וּמְבִיאִין אוֹתוֹ מִשָּׁם.
phrases.english: and the court sends for him and brings him from there.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁנִּתְחַיֵּיב מִיתָה בְּבֵית דִּין – הֲרָגוּהוּ,
phrases.english: One found liable for death in court, they executed him;
and one not found liable for death, they freed him.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁנִּתְחַיֵּיב גָּלוּת – מַחְזִירִין אוֹתוֹ לִמְקוֹמוֹ,
phrases.english: One found liable for exile, they return him to his place,
as it is stated: 'And the congregation shall return him'
'to his city of refuge, etc.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:25

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description of the ערי מקלט, now covering who runs there and what the court does afterward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every killer runs to an עיר מקלט first. The court brings him back for trial and executes him, frees him, or returns him to exile.

steps.title: משה and יהושע set up three cities each, lined up across from each other
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that משה set aside three cities east of the ירדן and יהושע set aside three matching cities in ארץ כנען. The two sets lined up like two rows in a vineyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: משה set aside three cities on the east side of the ירדן, and across from them יהושע set aside three in ארץ כנען. They were lined up like two rows in a vineyard: חברון on the mountain of יהודה across from בצר in the wilderness, שכם on the mountain of אפרים across from רמות in גלעד, and קדש on the mountain of נפתלי across from גולן in the בשן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that describes who chose the six cities and how they were placed. Each city in ארץ ישראל faced a matching city on the other side of the ירדן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the משנה's 'three across the ירדן and three in ארץ כנען.' It adds who chose each set (משה and יהושע) and their exact layout. The cities form three matching pairs, south, middle, and north, like vines planted in two straight rows.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside, chose as a city of refuge
The east side of the ירדן river
Lined up exactly across from each other
Two rows in a vineyard, a picture of two neat parallel lines

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁלֹשׁ עָרִים הִבְדִּיל מֹשֶׁה בְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן
phrases.english: Moshe set aside three cities on the east side of the Jordan,
and corresponding to them, Yehoshua set aside three in the land of Canaan,

phrases.aramaic: וּמְכֻוּוֹנוֹת הָיוּ כְּמִין שְׁתֵּי שׁוּרוֹת שֶׁבַּכֶּרֶם:
phrases.english: and they were lined up like two rows in a vineyard:

phrases.aramaic: חֶבְרוֹן בְּהַר יְהוּדָה כְּנֶגֶד בֶּצֶר בַּמִּדְבָּר,
phrases.english: Hebron on Mount Judah, opposite Bezer in the wilderness;

phrases.aramaic: שְׁכֶם בְּהַר אֶפְרַיִם כְּנֶגֶד רָמוֹת בַּגִּלְעָד,
phrases.english: Shechem on Mount Ephraim, opposite Ramoth in Gilead;

phrases.aramaic: קֶדֶשׁ בְּהַר נַפְתָּלִי כְּנֶגֶד גּוֹלָן בַּבָּשָׁן.
phrases.english: Kedesh on Mount Naphtali, opposite Golan in the Bashan.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שָׁלֹשׁ עָרִים הִבְדִּיל מֹשֶׁה בְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins with a ברייתא that expands on the משנה's statement about three cities on each side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה chose three cities east of the ירדן, and יהושע chose three matching cities in ארץ כנען. Each pair lined up across the river.

steps.title: The cities divide the land into four equal parts
steps.stepSummary: From the word 'ושלשת' the ברייתא learns that the three cities in ארץ ישראל must be spaced so they cut the land into four equal sections.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And you shall divide into three' means they must be evenly spaced. The distance from the southern border to חברון should equal the distance from חברון to שכם. The distance from חברון to שכם should equal the distance from שכם to קדש. And the distance from שכם to קדש should equal the distance from קדש to the northern border.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and learns from a פסוק how far apart the cities must be. The spacing has to be even all the way through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ושלשת is read as 'make three dividing points.' Three evenly spaced cities split the land into four equal stretches: border to חברון, חברון to שכם, שכם to קדש, and קדש to the border. This way no killer is ever too far from a city of refuge.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall divide into three,' from the פסוק about the cities of refuge
Evenly spaced, dividing the land into equal parts
South, here meaning the southern border of the land
North, here meaning the northern border of the land

phrases.english: 'And you shall divide into three': that they should be evenly divided,
phrases.notes: דברים 19:3

phrases.english: so that from the south to Hebron is like from Hebron to Shechem,
and from Hebron to Shechem is like from Shechem to Kedesh,
and from Shechem to Kedesh is like from Kedesh to the north.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, adding the rule for spacing the cities, learned from a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three cities in ארץ ישראל must divide the land into four equal stretches from south to north.

steps.title: Why does the small east side get as many cities as all of Israel?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the east side of the ירדן, where few tribes lived, got three cities, just like the much larger ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three on the east side of the ירדן, and three in ארץ ישראל?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the equal split of the cities. The east side was much smaller and had far fewer people, so why should it get the same number?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only two and a half tribes lived east of the ירדן, while more than nine tribes lived in ארץ ישראל. If the cities serve the people, you would expect fewer on the east side. The equal numbers seem unfair to the larger population.

phrases.english: On the east side of the Jordan, three,
and in Eretz Yisrael, three?!
phrases.notes: The surprise is that far more tribes lived in ארץ ישראל, yet it got the same number.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן תְּלָת, בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל תְּלָת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the even three-and-three split described in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The equal number of cities on both sides of the ירדן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The cities should match the population, but the small east side got as many as the much larger ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Killers were common in גלעד
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that murderers were common in גלעד, on the east side, so that side needed more cities of refuge.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: In גלעד, killers are common.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins to answer the question. More killings happened in גלעד, so the east side needed extra cities even though fewer people lived there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number of cities is set by how many killings happen, not by how many people live there. Since killers were common in גלעד, the east side needed as many cities as the larger land. The sentence continues past this point, so אביי is still explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: A region on the east side of the ירדן

phrases.english: Abaye said: In Gilead, killers are common,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why the east side got three cities.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual explanation: the need was based on how common killings were, not on population.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The number of cities should follow how many people live in each area.
steps.terutzMaskana: Killings were more common in גלעד, so the east side needed extra cities.
